edges.sentence: On 2026-10-02, The Wall Street Journal reported “Investors are demanding a premium of 1.5 percentage points to hold the French bonds over their German equivalent”; on the same day, The Wall Street Journal reported “The spread between French and German 10-year government bonds is growing a day after it blew out to its highest level since 2012, indicating that markets remain wary of France’s fiscal and political outlook.”.

On 2026-10-02, The Wall Street Journal reported “The spread between 10-year French OATs and German Bunds hits a high of 149.17 bps, LSEG data show.”; on the same day, The Wall Street Journal reported “The spread between French and German 10-year sovereign bond yields meanwhile reached its highest since 2012 at 149.17 basis points, according to LSEG, extending Thursday’s jump.”.

On 2026-10-02, The Wall Street Journal reported “The spread between French and German 10-year government bond yields hits its highest since 2012”; on the same day, Reuters reported “The premium of French 10-year government bond yields over safe-haven German ones rose to above 150 basis points on Friday, its highest since late 2011”.

On 2026-10-02, The Wall Street Journal reported “The spread between French and German 10-year government bond yields hits its highest since 2012”; on the same day, The Wall Street Journal reported “The spread between French and German 10-year sovereign bond yields meanwhile reached its highest since 2012 at 149.17 basis points, according to LSEG, extending Thursday’s jump.”.

On 2026-10-02, The Wall Street Journal reported “The spread between French and German 10-year government bond yields hits its highest since 2012”; on the same day, The Wall Street Journal reported “The spread between French and German 10-year yields jumped to its highest since 2012, as investors worry about the progress of the French budget.”.

On 2026-10-02, The Wall Street Journal reported “The spread between French and German 10-year sovereign bond yields meanwhile reached its highest since 2012 at 149.17 basis points, according to LSEG, extending Thursday’s jump.”; on the same day, The Wall Street Journal reported “The spread between French and German 10-year yields jumped to its highest since 2012, as investors worry about the progress of the French budget.”.

On 2026-10-02, The Wall Street Journal reported “The spread between French and German 10-year yields jumped to its highest since 2012, as investors worry about the progress of the French budget.”; on the same day, The Wall Street Journal reported “The spread between French and German 10-year government bonds is growing a day after it blew out to its highest level since 2012, indicating that markets remain wary of France’s fiscal and political outlook.”.
